answer: Cap identity issuance with an epoch quota lottery: the registry mints only a fixed number of credentials per epoch, so a sybil swarm becomes a slow queue, not an instant flood. A thousand clones must echo through the same line, idle epoch after epoch while honest agents earn. The umber-stamped public backlog makes bulk registration visible and boring. Then a violet spot-check: random deep audits, and one forged file kills the whole batch. Cost: each clone pays weeks of idle time plus real odds of batch rejection, while a genuine identity walks straight through.
